subject: Temporal SLO exception + commercial authorization request — Kairos Labs
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Matt Lang <matt.lang@kairoslabs.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Temporal SLO exception + commercial authorization request — Kairos Labs

Team,

Quick background: Kairos Labs (deal KAI-2027-149) is finalizing an enterprise contract for our Dedicated offering. They've signaled a hard production start on 2027-06-15 but their traffic profile indicates unpredictable bursts tied to end-of-day batch loads. They are asking for two non-standard items:

- A temporary SLO adjustment for the first 90 days of the contract: change availability target from 99.95% -> 99.7% for the Dedicated pool serving them (this would be timeboxed 2027-06-15 -> 2027-09-13).
- A higher service-credit cap for that window (from 10% annual cap -> up to 20% pro-rated for the 90-day period) and a one-time commercial concession (we're negotiating discount).

Attached: Kairos_SOW_v2.pdf (SOW with traffic profile) and SLO_amendment_redline.docx (proposed clause).

Why this matters: the customer's workload mixes near-realtime inference with heavy nightly reindexing. Our Dedicated pool can handle steady-state but initial ramp risks violating the tighter availability SLA. They are sensitive to terms because they will connect regulated downstream systems.

Ask: I need executive authorization to:
1) Approve the 90-day temporal SLO exception as drafted (see redline).
2) Approve a commercial concession up to 12% one-time discount (total contract value impact <= $150k) conditioned on (a) documented mitigation plan, (b) additional telemetry hooks, and (c) our right to revert to standard SLO after the window.

If authorized, we'll deliver an addendum and DocuSign link to the customer. Matt — please confirm you'd accept the timeboxed language and the one-time concession if approved.

Thanks,

Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Kairos_SOW_v2.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB)]
[Attachment: SLO_amendment_redline.docx (docx, 45KB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Matt Lang <matt.lang@kairoslabs.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-20T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Temporal SLO exception + commercial authorization request — Kairos Labs

Olga,

Thanks for the clear summary. I'm supportive of a timeboxed SLO relaxation if we can:
- Limit the concession to the specific Dedicated pool in the SOW (no platform-wide precedent).
- Add firm telemetry/alerting milestones (we should see baseline performance numbers by week 2).
- Tie the one-time discount to a commitment: 12 months minimum term and auto-escalation to standard pricing after the 90-day period.

Finance: please confirm the deal economics for a 12% concession (deal id KAI-2027-149). If finance signs off and Legal signs the redline, I'm comfortable recommending this to Sean for final signoff.

Marissa
VP, Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Temporal SLO exception + commercial authorization request — Kairos Labs

Marissa / team,

I've reviewed the redline. A few legal/ops notes we need captured before Sean signs:

1) Audit & logs: add a clause obligating Kairos to accept access-limited telemetry snapshots for the 90-day window and to allow a joint post-ramp review. This preserves our ability to demonstrate that any credit triggers were valid.
2) Data handling: confirm which datasets are in scope for retention rules (we should not broaden retention obligations in the addendum).
3) Liability: keep the service-credit construct isolated (no downstream indemnity expansion).

If those three items are inserted as short bullets in Section 3 of the amendment I can clear legal. I've attached an extract of suggested language into the redline doc.

Jonas
Head of Legal Ops
Redwood Inference

On 2027-05-20 10:04, Marissa Cole wrote:

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Matt Lang <matt.lang@kairoslabs.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-20T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Temporal SLO exception + commercial authorization request — Kairos Labs

All,

Engineering notes on mitigation and wording:
- We can deliver two immediate mitigations: (1) dedicated KV-cache priming during nightly reindex windows and (2) an autoscale buffer of +20% reserved capacity for the first 30 days. Both reduce the risk of availability dips but are operationally visible costs.
- Proposed SLA clause: when an SLO trigger occurs during the 90-day window, credits are calculated pro-rata on affected time slices (this keeps credit calculation bounded).
- We will add a preference for 'failover-to-variant' behavior on critical endpoints so customer-facing latency remains acceptable; documented in runbook.

From infra telemetry (last 30 days simulated): mean p95 latency under expected load 210ms, nightly batch peaks simulated to 2.4x baseline for short windows. The attached SOW has the load curves that drove our concession ask.

Ben Carter
Director, Site Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference
[Link: https://internal.redwood.com/telemetry/decks/kairos-sim-202705]

From: Matt Lang <matt.lang@kairoslabs.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-20T18:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Temporal SLO exception + commercial authorization request — Kairos Labs

Olga / team,

Thanks for the transparency and the proposed mitigations. We can accept a timeboxed SLO adjustment provided:
1) It is strictly limited to the Dedicated pool serving Kairos and ceases automatically after 90 days.
2) We receive the expanded telemetry snapshots and a biweekly checkpoint call for the first 60 days.
3) The one-time concession is applied to year-1 invoice as a line-item.

If you can get legal and your execs to sign by next Friday, we’ll proceed.

—Matt
CFO, Kairos Labs

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Matt Lang <matt.lang@kairoslabs.com>
Date: 2027-05-21T11:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Temporal SLO exception + commercial authorization request — Kairos Labs

All,

I've reviewed the summary, redlines from Legal, and the mitigation plan from SRE. I authorize the temporal SLO exception for the Dedicated pool serving Kairos Labs for the 90-day window (2027-06-15 -> 2027-09-13) with the following binding conditions:

- Maximum one-time commercial concession capped at 12% of year-1 ARR (not to exceed $150,000).
- Service-credit cap for the 90-day window increased to 20% pro-rated only for that period and calculated per affected time slice as proposed.
- Legal redlines (audit snapshots, retention scope, isolation of credits) must be inserted into the amendment before DocuSign.
- Engineering to enable the two mitigations (KV-cache priming + autoscale buffer) and provide the week-2 and week-4 telemetry checkpoints.

Olga — please proceed to finalize the addendum and route for DocuSign with the above conditions. Procurement (Matt) — expect the DocuSign by EOD Friday per your timeline if Legal and Finance are clear.

Sean Gallagher
Chief Revenue Officer
Redwood Inference

[Approved: exec note ID SG-2027-05-21-01]
